# Material selection (generated by cases/materials_study.py)

Stresses are the FEA's; for one material under applied loads they don't depend on its modulus, so each candidate's safety factor is its strength over the same peak. Temperatures are from `out/thermal/` (v3, the NEMA 34 at 50 % and 100 % of its 6.0 A).

## Sustained loads: creep, and the temperature each part runs at

| part | sustained stress (MPa) | where | at 50 % current: °C, PETG creep allowable (MPa), safety factor | at 100 % current: °C, PETG creep allowable (MPa), safety factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 carriage, vertical runs, creep | 3.04 | air | 26, 7.6, 2.49 | 39, 5.3, 1.73 |
| tensioner block, bearing bolts slipped | 3.10 | tensioner | 30, 6.7, 2.16 | 54, 2.6, 0.82 |
| A-1 screw head on its printed seat (snug) | 18.00 | air | 26, 7.6, 0.42 | 39, 5.3, 0.29 |
| A-1 screw head with a DIN 433 washer | 15.00 | air | 26, 7.6, 0.50 | 39, 5.3, 0.35 |
| paternoster gondola, hanging | 0.49 | room | 22, 8.2, 16.68 | 22, 8.2, 16.68 |

PETG's 8 MPa (1000 h, room temperature) is derated here in proportion to how far the part sits below PETG HF's 69 °C HDT, falling to zero at it. That is a rule of thumb, not creep data. The practical rule is to keep a part under sustained load 20 K or more below its HDT: about 49 °C for PETG, 80 °C for ASA, 97 °C for PC and over 150 °C for the CF nylons and PET-CF.

## Candidates

| material | HDT 0.45 MPa (°C) | across layers (MPa) | $/kg | moisture | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PETG HF | 69 | 23 | 20 | low | the baseline; tough, cheap, easy |
| PLA | 57 | see its TDS | 20 | low | creeps at 40 C and brittle: not for this rig |
| ABS | 87 | see its TDS | 22 | low | warps on a large flat part like the 351 mm carriage |
| ASA | 100 | see its TDS | 28 | low | ABS's heat resistance, warps less; UV-stable |
| PC | 117 | see its TDS | 35 | moderate | tough and hot; stress-crazes with IPA or acetone under load |
| PAHT-CF | 194 | 47 | 80 | high: dry it before printing; about 1/3 stiffer dry than wet | far less creep; needs a hardened nozzle (the H2D has one); conductive fibres, but not ESD-rated |
| PET-CF | 205 | see its TDS | 75 | low | the stiff, hot, dimensionally stable option; brittle in impact |
| ESD PETG (carbon-loaded) | 69 | see its TDS | 45 | low | 10^6-10^9 ohm/sq: lets charge drain from parts that touch powder |

## v4's back plate: 6061 or steel

Modes with the back side plate in 1/4 in steel: 14.9, 22.5, 27.2, 59.7, 86.8, 96.9 Hz (6061: 15.2, 22.9, 29.7, 50.6, 80.3, 81.1). The plate weighs 8.46 kg instead of 2.9 kg.
